title: Cockpit Panel Harnesses — Windshield Heating and Glareshield Run

ata.title: Flight Compartment Wiring — Cockpit Panel Harnesses

abstract: Wiring sheet for the cockpit panel harnesses behind the glareshield, including the windshield heating supply from the circuit breaker panel to the pane terminal block and its tail at the outboard terminal position.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the cockpit panel harness run behind the glareshield and the side consoles, including the windshield heating supply from the circuit breaker panel to the pane terminal block.
sections.sheet_note: One harness tail route is shown for the windshield heating: from the frame penetration to the outboard terminal position on the pane terminal block. The heating supply is 115 V AC and shares a raceway with low-level signal wiring for part of the run; the separation distance in that raceway is given on the sheet and is not a general standard practice value. Tail lengths are cut to the dimension on the sheet and are not adjustable at installation, because the strain relief boss is moulded into the backshell.
sections.routing_note: The harness leaves the circuit breaker panel at the overhead, runs forward above the glareshield to the pane position, and drops to the terminal block through the frame penetration with a silicone edging grommet. The drop is vertical from the grommet to the outboard terminal, so the tail leaves the backshell straight and no bend radius case arises at the terminal itself.

ata.title: Flight Compartment Wiring — Cockpit Panel Harnesses

abstract: Wiring sheet for the cockpit panel harnesses behind the glareshield, including the windshield heating supply and its terminal tail, whose route changes with the improved terminal block position.

sections.purpose: This sheet shows the cockpit panel harness run behind the glareshield and the side consoles, including the windshield heating supply from the circuit breaker panel to the pane terminal block.
sections.sheet_note: Two harness tail routes are shown for the windshield heating: the original route to the outboard terminal position and the revised route to the terminal position moved 22 mm inboard. Both are live standards in the fleet and the sheet must be read with the aircraft standard in mind. The heating supply is 115 V AC and shares a raceway with low-level signal wiring for part of the run; the separation distance in that raceway is given on the sheet and is not a general standard practice value.
sections.routing_note: The harness leaves the circuit breaker panel at the overhead, runs forward above the glareshield to the pane position, and drops to the terminal block through the frame penetration with a silicone edging grommet. The revised route takes the drop 22 mm inboard, which changes the grommet position and shortens the tail by 40 mm. A tail cut for the original route will not reach the revised terminal position. The second terminal is the critical one: with the block moved inboard and the grommet left where it was, the tail would turn through 28 mm of radius against a 45 mm minimum for AWG 10 in this insulation. The grommet therefore moves inboard with the block, which is what holds the radius at 52 mm. Neither the grommet position nor the tail length may be changed without the other.
